notable_absence.finding: No Enterprise/Community edition badge and no server-version-string citation appear anywhere on this page (both known recurring anomalies absent here, as expected for a concept-overview page). More notably for this batch's hypothesis: this page never mentions storage engines (Couchstore/Magma) at all, even though it is the top-level 'Manage Your Data' / bucket-concepts page - the storage-engine choice is deferred entirely to storage-engines.md and manage-buckets.md (bucket creation), confirming storage engine is documented as a property of an individual bucket, not of the Data Service itself.

cross_component_finding: This page states hard numeric ceilings not seen elsewhere in the registry slice reviewed: a maximum of 30 buckets per cluster, and up to 1000 scopes and 1000 collections per cluster. It also draws a clean two-axis role split that recurs across this whole batch: bucket/scope/collection *administration* (create/modify/delete) is gated by Project Owner or Cluster Manager, while *data access* within those same resources (documents) is gated by a different role pair, Data Reader/Data Writer - confirmed directly in manage-documents.json and import-data-documents.json (this batch). The phrase 'the _Couchbase_ bucket type' (with 'Couchbase' scoped as a specific type name) implies at least one other bucket type exists; export.md (this batch) independently confirms this by naming 'the Memory Only bucket type' as excluded from cluster-backup coverage - a bucket-*type* axis (Couchbase vs Memory Only) distinct from the bucket-*storage-engine* axis (Couchstore vs Magma) that storage-engines.md documents.
